item.title: A painful homecoming: Zandile and daughters return to Bulawayo
item.description: Bongani Ndlovu, Sunday News Reporter THE Khumalo family will today receive the remains of their daughter, Nothabo Zandile Tshuma (née Khumalo) and her two daughters, Nala and Natalie, at the Joshua Mqabuko Nkomo International Airport in Bulawayo, marking a step towards finding closure following the devastating tragedy that claimed their lives in the United Kingdom. The bodies are expected to arrive at the airport at 2 pm after departing from the United Kingdom yesterday and making a stopover in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, before continuing their journey to Zimbabwe. Speaking on behalf of the family, Mr Leon Leroy Khumalo said all arrangements were in place for the arrival of their loved ones, with family members set to gather at the airport to receive them. “All is in place for us to receive our daughter Zandile and our grandchildren, Nala and Natalie at the Joshua Mqabuko Nkomo International Airport on Sunday. The family will be at the airport to receive the bodies when they land at 2 pm,” said Mr Khumalo. [caption id=attachment_5394356 align=alignnone width=1024] Ndodana Tshuma[/caption] He said the family would hold a meeting at home upon the arrival to discuss the way forward as they prepare to lay their loved ones to rest. “We shall have a meeting at home to see how best we are receiving the bodies. The MP for Luveve will be at hand as we help each other,” he said. The repatriation of the bodies marks an important step for the family, who have been waiting for the process to be completed so that they can give Zandile and her daughters a dignified farewell in their homeland. Mr Khumalo previously said the family’s wish was for the three to be buried in Zimbabwe, where relatives and friends could come together to mourn and find closure following the tragedy. The family said the three would be buried on Tuesday side by side at Old Luveve Cemetery after a funeral service at Brethren in Christ Church in New Lobengula, with their bodies briefly passing through the family home in Gwabalanda. On Thursday, more than 500 mourners gathered in Bedford, United Kingdom, to remember Zandile and her daughters, Natalie and Nala. A remembrance service was held at Bedford’s Corn Exchange, where family, friends, colleagues and members of the community paid tribute to the 42-year-old mother and her two daughters, aged 15 and five. Tributes described Zandile as a devoted mother who nurtured and cared for those around her, while her daughters were remembered for their kindness and bright personalities. Natalie’s school headmistress described her as a thoughtful pupil whose smile reflected the person she was. Zandile and her daughters Natalie, 15 and Nala, five, were found dead at their home in Great Denham, Bedfordshire, United Kingdom, in July after concerns were raised when they had not been seen for several days. A murder investigation was launched by Bedfordshire Police, with Zandile’s husband, Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma, 45, becoming the prime suspect. He was later arrested in South Africa following an international manhunt. Forensic post-mortem examinations in the UK found that the three died from blunt force trauma. Tshuma appeared before the Johannesburg Magistrates’ Court after his arrest and was initially charged in South Africa with unlawful possession of a firearm as authorities began the process of determining his extradition to the UK, where he faces murder allegations. His case was postponed as authorities worked through legal processes related to his status and extradition proceedings. The tragedy has attracted widespread attention in Zimbabwe and the United Kingdom, with tributes pouring in for Zandile and her daughters from relatives, friends, schools and the wider community. (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews

item.title: President declares South Africa bus tragedy State of Disaster
item.description: Sunday News Reporter PRESIDENT Mnangagwa has declared the tragic Munhenzva Transport Services bus accident in Trompsburg, Free State Province, South Africa, which claimed the lives of 11 Zimbabwean nationals a State of Disaster. The declaration was made in terms of Section 27(1) of the Civil Protection Act [Chapter 10:06] to enable Government to mobilise resources and coordinate assistance for the affected families and survivors. In a statement yesterday, Local Government and Public Works Minister Daniel Garwe said the accident occurred last Friday involving a Munhenzva bus travelling from Cape Town to Harare. “As at 1 August 2026, the incident has claimed the lives of 11 Zimbabwean nationals, comprising one adult male, five adult females and five minors,” said Minister Garwe. [caption id=attachment_4928975 align=aligncenter width=680] Minister Daniel Garwe[/caption] He said several other passengers were injured and were receiving medical treatment at Pelonomi and Universitas Hospitals in Bloemfontein. Minister Garwe said the declaration would allow Government to coordinate interventions, including repatriation of the deceased, assistance to survivors and provision of humanitarian support to affected families. “The declaration of a State of Disaster enables Government to mobilise the necessary resources and coordinate interventions in support of the affected families. This includes facilitating the repatriation of the deceased, assisting survivors and providing appropriate humanitarian assistance to all those impacted by this tragic incident,” he said. President Mnangagwa conveyed his condolences to families who lost their loved ones and wished injured passengers a speedy recovery. “His Excellency, President Mnangagwa, has conveyed his deepest condolences to the bereaved families and extended his heartfelt sympathies to all those who have lost loved ones. He has further wished those who are injured a swift and full recovery,” said Minister Garwe. Government also commended South African authorities, emergency services, healthcare workers, and Zimbabwean diplomatic officials for their response following the accident. The Civil Protection Department, working with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Trade, the Zimbabwe Embassy in South Africa and other stakeholders, has been tasked with coordinating the repatriation of the deceased and assistance to injured survivors. “Government will continue to keep the nation informed as further verified information becomes available,” said Minister Garwe. (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews

item.title: NODE earns continental recognition for community empowerment drive @ZANUPF_Official
item.description: Gibson Mhaka THE National Organisation for Development and Empowerment (NODE), a Zanu-PF affiliate, has received continental recognition after being honoured at the prestigious iChange Nations Africa Awards held recently in Victoria Falls for its contribution to community empowerment and socio-economic transformation. The recognition places the organisation among a select group of African institutions acknowledged for advancing community development, ethical leadership and initiatives that improve the livelihoods of ordinary citizens. The accolade comes as Zimbabwe accelerates efforts towards attaining Vision 2030, with organisations such as NODE complementing Government programmes aimed at empowering communities in line with President Mnangagwa’s development philosophy of leaving no one and no place behind. The awards ceremony brought together former Heads of State, diplomats, traditional leaders, Government officials, development practitioners and civil society representatives from across the continent to celebrate institutions and individuals making a positive impact in their respective countries. Receiving the award on behalf of the organisation, NODE Bulawayo provincial chairman Mr Eddie Benson Muchenje described the honour as a significant endorsement of the organisation’s commitment to improving the welfare of vulnerable communities through empowerment and sustainable development initiatives. To NODE, this award is an assurance that the Vision 2030 mantra is achievable through the philosophy of leaving no one and no place behind. We sincerely appreciate the guidance of our mentor, His Excellency President Mnangagwa, whose vision continues to inspire us to serve communities through empowerment and development, he said. Mr Muchenje said the recognition would motivate the organisation to expand programmes that promote patriotism, self-reliance and economic empowerment, particularly among young people. Every citizen has a responsibility to cultivate patriotism and love for Zimbabwe, especially among the youth, who remain the country’s future leaders. We believe empowering young people economically and socially is one of the most effective ways of building a prosperous nation, he said. Founded in 2012, NODE has grown into a nationwide empowerment organisation with a presence across Zimbabwe as well as in neighbouring South Africa and Botswana. Its programmes target women, youths, people living with disabilities and other vulnerable groups through initiatives designed to enhance livelihoods, promote entrepreneurship and encourage sustainable community development. Mr Muchenje said the organisation was established to complement national development efforts by addressing socio-economic challenges confronting communities. NODE was founded in 2012 out of a desire to uplift communities by responding to the challenges affecting ordinary Zimbabweans while supporting His Excellency President Mnangagwa’s vision of inclusive national development, he said. He said his involvement with NODE evolved from supporting its programmes to assuming leadership of the Bulawayo province after appreciating the impact the organisation was making in communities. I was first drawn to NODE because of its commitment to community service and patriotism. As I became more involved, I realised that its programmes were helping transform lives while complementing the national development agenda. When I was entrusted with leading the Bulawayo province, I accepted the responsibility with humility and determination, he said. Beyond humanitarian assistance, Mr Muchenje said the organisation had shifted its focus towards sustainable empowerment by equipping beneficiaries with practical skills capable of generating long-term income. He said instead of creating dependency through donations alone, NODE was empowering communities through vocational skills, entrepreneurship and income-generating projects. We want people to become economically independent. Through skills development in sectors such as agriculture, mining, fabrication and steelwork, beneficiaries are equipped to earn sustainable incomes, support their families and contribute meaningfully to the country’s economic growth, he said. Mr Muchenje said the organisation was also broadening its developmental footprint by pursuing projects capable of transforming communities and creating opportunities for young people. Our vision extends beyond welfare programmes. We are engaging partners on projects that promote infrastructure development, youth empowerment and affordable housing, particularly for self-employed entrepreneurs and small business owners who often struggle to access decent accommodation, he said. He added that NODE had intensified its anti-drug and substance abuse campaigns through its Identify-Rehabilitate-Empower model, which seeks to rehabilitate affected youths before integrating them into productive economic activities. The organisation has also undertaken several community-based social responsibility programmes, including providing assistance to vulnerable groups. Last December, it brought festive cheer to 143 inmates at Anju Farm Prison in Matabeleland North through a Christmas outreach initiative that underscored its commitment to ensuring that no segment of society is left behind. The iChange Nations Africa Awards form part of a global movement that recognises institutions and individuals whose work advances humanity through ethical leadership, community development, humanitarian service and public service. This year’s recipients included Deputy Minister of Tourism and Hospitality Industry Tongai Mnangagwa, Minister of State for Matabeleland North Provincial Affairs and Devolution Richard Moyo, Senator Chief Fortune Charumbira, former Mauritian President Professor Ameenah Gurib-Fakim, former African Union Commission chairperson Dr Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma and Nelson Mandela Foundation chief executive officer Dr Sello Hatang, among other distinguished African leaders. For NODE, the continental recognition not only celebrates achievements recorded over the past decade but also affirms the growing role of community-based organisations in complementing Government efforts to build an empowered, inclusive and prosperous Zimbabwe. (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews

item.title: 2026 Chibuku Neshamwari Traditional Dance Festival roars to life
item.description: Mthabisi Tshuma in Harare THE 2026 Chibuku Neshamwari Traditional Dance Festival has burst into life at Harare Gardens, with 10 of Zimbabwe’s finest traditional dance ensembles competing for the coveted national title and a US$15 000 grand prize. The annual festival, organised by Delta Corporation through its flagship Chibuku brand in partnership with the National Arts Council of Zimbabwe (NACZ) and the Zimbabwe National Traditional Dance Association (ZNTDA), has drawn performers and cultural enthusiasts from across the country’s 10 provinces. [caption id=attachment_5428778 align=aligncenter width=300] 2026 Chibuku Neshamwari Traditional Dance Festival[/caption] The winning group will walk away with US$15 000, while the first and second runners-up will receive US$10 000 and US$7 500 respectively. Representing Matabeleland South is Bolamba Culture Birds, while Bulawayo is represented by Ezimnyama Dance Ensemble. Matabeleland North has fielded Amakhosikazi Dance Ensemble. Other contestants are Shingai Dance Group (Harare), Dapuraunanzva Arts Ensemble (Manicaland), Marondera Gure Club (Mashonaland East), Pisa Pisa Nyau Club (Mashonaland West), Dzimbahwe Nengoma Dance Ensemble (Mashonaland Central), Chipolopolo Nyau Dance Group (Midlands) and Mutimurefu School of Arts (MUSA) from Masvingo. [caption id=attachment_5428773 align=aligncenter width=300] 2026 Chibuku Neshamwari Traditional Dance Festival[/caption] Beyond the energetic performances on stage, Harare Gardens has been transformed into a vibrant celebration of Zimbabwean culture, with festival-goers taking part in traditional games that have added to the festive atmosphere. Attendees have been reliving childhood memories through indigenous games such as tsoro and pads, creating a family-friendly environment that celebrates the country’s rich cultural heritage. [caption id=attachment_5428783 align=aligncenter width=300] 2026 Chibuku Neshamwari Traditional Dance Festival[/caption] The festival is expected to conclude with a star-studded after-party headlined by Jah Prayzah, supported by Baba Harare, Nisha Ts and Chillspot Records duo DJ Fantan and Levels. The Chibuku Neshamwari Traditional Dance Festival remains one of Zimbabwe’s premier cultural events, providing a platform for preserving and promoting the country’s diverse traditional dances while rewarding artistic excellence. Follow on X: @mthabisi_mthire (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews
